intro: Wallingford is a market town on the Thames in south Oxfordshire, still ringed on its west side by the grassy banks of a Saxon town wall. Inside them lies the Kinecroft, an open green, and at its edge a great horse chestnut towers over the Coach and Horses pub. A reader sent us its photograph and told us it is due to be felled soon.

trees.name: The Horse Chestnut of the Coach and Horses
trees.age_estimate: 150 to 180 years, by a reader's estimate

location.address: Behind the Coach and Horses, Kinecroft, Wallingford, Oxfordshire

trees.story:
On the edge of the Kinecroft, the open green inside Wallingford's old Saxon earth walls, a horse chestnut has grown so close to the Coach and Horses that it seems to rise out of the pub itself. A reader sent us this photograph from the grass, and wrote that the tree "has grown immediately adjacent and to an extent from the ground of The Coach and Horses public house."

The picture shows a tree far bigger than the building. A thick grey trunk stands right against the pub's back wall, and above the roof and chimney its crown opens into a huge dome of bare branches, wider than the whole frontage and twice its height. The reader puts it at 150 to 180 years old; that figure is theirs.

It may not be here for long. "Sadly it is due to be cut down in the immediate future," the reader wrote, "hence the temporary fencing in the photo." Wallingford Town Council called it a prominent tree of significant landscape value in 2022, while reporting that it was declining with a fungal disease and had structural defects that shorten its safe life.

If you want to see it, go soon, and stand on the Kinecroft where the reader stood. If it has already come down, tell us here and we will take it off the map.

question_meta: The great horse chestnut over the Coach and Horses on Wallingford's Kinecroft, due to be felled: where it stands and what we know.
question_answer: The Horse Chestnut of the Coach and Horses stands against the back of the Coach and Horses pub on the Kinecroft, the open green in Wallingford, Oxfordshire. It is seen from the green, which is free and open.
question_context: A reader who photographed this tree from the Kinecroft in Wallingford sent it to us with a warning: it is due to be cut down in the immediate future, which is why temporary fencing stands along the front of the pub. The tree is a horse chestnut that has grown right beside the Coach and Horses, and to an extent from its ground, in the reader's words. In the photograph its bare crown rises far above the brick building and its chimney and spreads past both ends of it, a dome of branches twice the height of the pub. The reader puts it at 150 to 180 years old; that figure is theirs. Wallingford Town Council wrote in 2022 that it is a prominent tree of significant landscape value, and that it was reported to be declining with a fungal disease and had structural defects shortening its safe life. The Kinecroft is an open green inside the town's old Saxon earth walls, and the best view of the tree is from the grass in front of the pub. Go soon if you want to see it standing.

faq.q: Where is the big horse chestnut in Wallingford?
faq.a: Against the back of the Coach and Horses pub, on the edge of the Kinecroft green inside the town's Saxon walls.

faq.q: Can I visit The Horse Chestnut of the Coach and Horses?
faq.a: Yes, you see it from the Kinecroft, a free public green. The pub's garden is fenced off for now.

faq.q: Is the Wallingford horse chestnut being cut down?
faq.a: A reader told us in November 2026 that it is due to be felled soon, and fencing was up around it. If it has gone, tell us and we will take it off the map.
